column8: Wed 18 Nov: References and 2.5, the most citable Charles Ellis read at source (FAJ 1975; the rater re-read the line at archive.org); it is advice to managers trying to win, so cite it for playing by one's own written policy (2.5's adherence check), never for protect you from yourself; pairs with Q46-008 from the same article.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.5 or 3f, one clause at most beside Q17-031's 11 of 200 trades and $200 (NUMBERS 8m); quote re-read at source by the rater; Ellis assumed 3% a trade, so the point is fewer decisions, never cost saved or a WInS result; near Q46-008 and H8-077.

Wed 18 Nov: store only; the quote is real (re-read at source by the rater) but Ellis means where research time goes, not a dated sale, so never cite him for the 2031 move; keep the quote, drop the link to l.15.

Wed 18 Nov: store, or 3f as a source on who decides (Caplet advises, Laura accepts); Ellis 1979 rests on its abstract only, Stockton's communication link re-read at source by the rater; read the 1979 body before any quote.

Wed 18 Nov: store only; the famous line comes from Ellis's books through reviews and a forum in three wordings, no edition read at source, so S 2 and never quoted until ch.13 is read with an edition and page; CFA 2010 (row 15) carries the same job at source.
Wed 18 Nov: store, or 3f; Ellis's own spoken words on the behavioural job, read at source; a podcast remark, never a definition of an IPS; a usable Ellis reference while the books stay unread.

Wed 18 Nov: store, possibly 3f; Ellis's one-sheet test fits a 500-word IPS, but never claim the IPS passed a reader test or that no word would change (the report evaluates it); his yearly re-read is not added (A34).

Wed 18 Nov: 3e, re-read at source by the rater: Ellis expects a policy to change in its details, so l.17's only is stricter than the practice's founder; pairs with rows 33-34; the details named in advance (l.13's fund or bond, the top-up's size) are evaluation, never new rules.

Wed 18 Nov: 3.0 or 3f, Ellis's ten-year test (re-read at source by the rater) with fi360's competent third party, a frame for judging the IPS; fix two claims: a stranger needs the IPS plus the report's written rules (the extra Treasuries, the range rule, Table 3), not l.11-l.15 alone; and say no planned investment decision after January 2028 except the 2031 move, since a fund closing early is Table 3 row 4's watch.
Wed 18 Nov: store; Ellis's second test, re-read at source by the rater; co-sponsors never run the portfolio, so a loose parallel; Laura in 2031 living with the 2026 choice is the usable half.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.2's the allocation is the rule, not a target mix, with a vivid outside voice (re-read at source by the rater); fix before use: say allocation bands and paraphrase Ellis, never quote his ranges in a report whose 2031 promise is a dollar range.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.5, Ellis on recording the why (re-read at source by the rater), beside H9-178; the record is 15 notes on 11 filled trades, four of them on cancelled orders (23 Oct snapshot), so say each filled trade carries its written reason.

Wed 18 Nov: store only; This is a pledge is the interviewer's (Nikki Kraus) and a vehicle for good thinking is Ellis's, both seen at source; the should-be-changed line was not seen; never borrow pledge, which 3d keeps for money owed rather than owned (H7-070).

Wed 18 Nov: store; an FAJ abstract for Ellis on staying with a program; in his account the steadying is a consultant's job, in Laura's plan mostly the bonds' (row 18); body not read, so quote the abstract only.

Wed 18 Nov: a correction to Q7-020, re-read at source by the rater: the CFA sentence opens Perhaps most importantly, so any quote of it carries the ranking words; the standard's own hedge is the honest form of claim 1.
Wed 18 Nov: store only; Trone is quoted through a consultant's PDF and his books were not read, so S 2 and never quoted; Allodium's wish-not-a-plan line is a slogan, not a reference.
Wed 18 Nov: store, a coherence fact for 2.0 or 3e at most: fi360's market noise (re-read at source by the rater) is the word TNA l.15 used; point to TNA l.15, never repeat it.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.0 or 3.0, claim 1's answer; fix: the calming job also covers the half of VT kept after the move (l.15), not only VT before it; attribute the first job to CFA 2010 and fi360 read at source, never to Ellis's books (row 5).
Wed 18 Nov: a guard for writers: never say the IPS matters more than the assets; choosing bonds held to their end is the commitment.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.5's frame, re-read at source by the rater: liability turns on process, not performance, as Wharton's rule that WInS gains are never evidence; near Q34-019; never carry the word prudent onto the plan or the range rule.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.5, the test a public reviewer applies (2256.006(b), re-read at source by the rater): each decision against the written policy, judged across all funds; a model of a review, never law that binds Laura; pairs with row 22.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.5's form with an outside precedent (TWDB re-read at source by the rater): a state audit tested adherence to the written policy, found no discrepancies and never tested returns; the report borrows the form (criterion, test, result) and never claims it was audited.

Wed 18 Nov: store only; fix a false fact before any use: the team record says from 7 Oct only one team member placed or cancelled orders, never that one placed every order (PEOPLE_IN_THE_ROOM); training and broker checks have no use for Laura.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.3 (or 2.0), evidence for spine row 2, re-read at source by the rater (2256.005(d)): suitability to what the money must pay ranks first, diversification fifth, yield last, so a matched ladder answers why so few holdings; say ranks, never that the law approves the plan; the statute still asks a policy to address diversification, and VT diversifies the money not promised.

Wed 18 Nov: Table 1's note at most, re-read at source by the rater: a public report states each asset's maturity, a precedent for the Pays for column already planned; a presentation choice, never a rule.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.5, answers a judge's what about returns: performance is judged against objectives (fi360 4.1.1, re-read at source by the rater), and the ladder's objective is each payment covered (Q17-018, Q17-019); VT is never benchmarked on its WInS return.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e or 2.2, re-read at source by the rater: the CFA standard asks an IPS to document a choice not to rebalance, and Caplet's does in two lines (l.13, l.17; CANON A33); an evaluation that adds no rule.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e and Table 3, a legal anchor for why a hold-to-the-end plan still watches (Wharton asks what to monitor as 2031 and 2033 approach); Laura is not a trust, so a parallel only; never carry prudent onto the plan.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e, the objection a judge could raise (a ladder on auto pilot) with its reply in Table 3; fi360's words re-read at source by the rater; calendar reviews stay out (A34); beside Q15-013.
Wed 18 Nov: store only; process audits are an industry, but a paid certification adds nothing a judge needs and must never suggest the plan is certified.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.5, NUMBERS 8m's table in the auditors' form (row 22); figures match 8m and Q17-031; the record is 15 notes on 11 filled trades, four on cancelled orders, so say each filled trade has its note; mostly restates SKELETON 2.5, so not F 4.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e or 3c, judged by date and order while the market sets only the size (near aha row 4); fix the 2028 order: the top-up, then the extra Treasuries, then the floor, then VT (NUMBERS 2; the order-of-purchase reserve), not ten, floor, VT.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e, a candidate aha with row 34 (SCERA, Akron and Stockton re-read at source by the rater): the market carve-out is the IPS world's boilerplate, and CFA 2010 itself warns that templates sacrifice the investor's own factors; say six of seven read, never every IPS; test it cold before it takes a slot.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e, the evaluation of l.17 a judge will not expect: the closed list, not the carve-out, is rare (seven read; Akron re-read by the rater); the reasons to change are exits for when the plan cannot be carried out, never the ways a promise fails, and never only two things can break the plan (Q109).

Wed 18 Nov: 3e evidence for row 34, re-read at source by the rater: 12 revisions from Feb 2019 to Jul 2026, 8 by Jul 2021, about 1.6 a year (Keel arithmetic), triennial reviews among them; a many-manager pension, so the contrast is in kind, not a fault.
Wed 18 Nov: store; change by procedure (nine drafts, three approvals) against l.17's change by event; one clause at most, behind row 35.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e, re-read at source by the rater: two of Akron's four triggers are open-ended; l.17's two can be checked, but 31 March 2028 and five business days are Table 3's readings (Keel's call, Q8b-028), never the IPS's definition.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e, the plan's design in one contrast (re-read at source by the rater; quote extended in lowercase, mid-sentence): Stockton reviews a hired manager after bad returns; Laura has no manager chosen for skill and a bond held to its end pays the same after a fall; second to rows 33-34 for 3e's space.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e limits, the honest silence: l.17 says nothing on Laura's own goals changing (Q77); fix most: two of the seven read (UNE, Akron) tie review to the client's needs, so say some; note the silence and add no rule (A34).
Wed 18 Nov: store; most of what l.17 gives up is machinery Laura has no use for, but fund sponsors can still close or merge funds (Table 3 row 4), so never say nothing needs watching.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e's sentence on l.17, the evaluation the report owes (what a closed list gains and gives up) in place of repeating it; Keel's synthesis of rows 33-40; Laura keeps her legal power to change (Q7), and never only two things can break the plan.

Wed 18 Nov: store, or 3e as one evaluation clause: by the UK's 1995 list the IPS covers kinds, balance, risk and realisation and states no expected return (the 7.5% is J.P. Morgan's, TNA l.23, above the middle of published forecasts, never the top or the consensus); near H3-063.
